summary: The Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Research and Control Amendments Act of 2025 extends and modifies federal programs through fiscal year 2030 to research, monitor, forecast, and mitigate harmful algal blooms and hypoxia across marine, estuarine, and freshwater systems in the United States. It updates the duties of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Environmental Protection Agency, expands the Inter-Agency Task Force on Harmful Algal Blooms to include the Department of Energy, and establishes a national observation network and incubator program.

key_provisions: Extends appropriations through fiscal year 2030, authorizing $19,500,000 annually for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and $8,000,000 annually for the Environmental Protection Agency.
Requires the Inter-Agency Task Force on Harmful Algal Blooms to submit an action strategy to Congress at least once every five years, and adds the Department of Energy to the task force.
Directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to establish a national network of observing systems for monitoring, detecting, and forecasting harmful algal blooms.

Directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, in collaboration with the Environmental Protection Agency and research institutions, to establish a national-level incubator program to fund and test novel prevention, mitigation, and control strategies.
Requires the Environmental Protection Agency to develop and enhance operational freshwater harmful algal bloom monitoring, observing, and forecasting programs in lakes, rivers, and reservoirs.

Authorizes $2,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for events of national significance, including the ability for federal officials to waive non-Federal share requirements and provide grants for impacted entities.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Harmful Algal Bloom and Hypoxia Research and Control Amendments Act of 2025 extends and modifies federal programs through fiscal year 2030 to research, monitor, forecast, and mitigate harmful algal blooms and hypoxia across marine, estuarine, and freshwater systems in the United States. It updates the duties of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Environmental Protection Agency, expands the Inter-Agency Task Force on Harmful Algal Blooms to include the Department of Energy, and establishes a national observation network and incubator program.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation represents a multi-year reauthorization and expansion of federal programs governing water quality, ecological monitoring, and research into toxic algae and oxygen-depleted water zones. By broadening the scope from coastal waters to include freshwater systems, incorporating additional agencies, establishing new observation networks, and authorizing millions in funding through 2030, the bill alters how federal, state, and tribal entities coordinate to manage environmental and public health risks related to algal blooms.
